verses.1: And Rehobam went forth, for all of Israel had come to choose him as their king.
verses.2: And it happened that Jerubbaal, son of Nebat, heard about Egypt. He had fled from King Solomon. So Jerubbaal returned from Egypt.
verses.3: And they sent for him. He came in, along with all of Israel. They spoke to Rehoboam, saying:
verses.4: Your father made our lives difficult. Now, please ease the burden of your father’s hard work and the heavy responsibilities he placed upon us. We will serve you instead.
verses.5: And he said to them, “In three days, come back to me again.” Then the people went away.
verses.6: And King Rehoboam asked the elders who stood before Solomon, his father, during his lifetime, what they suggested as a way to return the people’s favor.
verses.7: And they said to him, “If it is good for this people, and if you truly desire to speak to them in a good manner, then may they become your servants forever.”
verses.8: And he abandoned the advice of the elders who had advised him, and he also abandoned the advice of the children who had grown up under his care.
verses.9: And he said to them, “What are you suggesting? What do you want to do with this people who have spoken to me and said, ‘Let’s be less generous than our father was to us.’”
verses.10: And the children who grew up with him said to him, “Say this to the people who have spoken to you: ‘Your father burdened us with heavy responsibilities, but you, on the other hand, are light-hearted compared to us.’” So he said to them, “Children, I am heavier in burden than my father.”
verses.11: And now, my father has burdened you with heavy loads. I will add to your burdens even more. My father will take them away from you through suffering. And I will be the one who carries those burdens.
verses.12: And Jerubbaal and all the people went to Rehobam on the third day, when the king said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
verses.13: And the king replied harshly. Then King Rehoboam abandoned the advice of the elders.
verses.14: And he spoke to them with the advice of the children, saying, “I will punish you. My father will remove you from here by force. I will be your enemy.”
verses.15: And the king did not hear from the people, because they were away from God, in order for Jehovah to carry out what He had spoken through His brother Shelobni to Jerubbaal, son of Nebat.
verses.16: And all of Israel said, “The king has not listened to them. So the people rebelled against the king and said, ‘What share do we have in David’s kingdom? It must not be given to the son of Jesse. Now, see your house, David! All of Israel went to their own homes.”
verses.17: And the children of Israel, who lived in the cities of Judah, were ruled by Rehoboam.
verses.18: And King Rehobam sent Hadoram to carry out this task. The children of Israel used stones to kill him. King Rehobam then rushed up onto the chariot to go to Jerusalem.
verses.19: And Israel sinned in the house of David, up to this very day.
